# DKR-010: No container mounts the Docker socket

- **Group:** Docker
- **Severity when it fails:** critical
- **Root:** the full result needs `sudo`. Without root this check may report `unknown`; it never reports a pass it could not verify.

## Why it matters

A container with the Docker socket, or a folder that holds it (/var/run, /run, /var, /), can start a privileged container and own the host. A read only bind does not help: the socket accepts writes through it. Reverse proxies, PaaS agents and socket proxies need the socket and warn instead of failing, with the reason shown; they are still root on the host if compromised. A bind of a folder that holds the socket says so (for example / read only): a read only mount does not stop a process from connecting to the socket. A bind of / or /var passes when another mount provably hides the whole socket folder inside the container: a tmpfs, a volume or a bind of an unrelated host folder exactly on its run folder (for example a tmpfs on /rootfs/run over / at /rootfs, since the host's /var/run is a link to /run). The result names the mount that masks it. A bind of /run, /var/run or the socket file is never masked, since covering the socket alone leaves the rest of /run in view; an unknown mount type, a path with . or .. in it, or a covering bind from a relative path or /proc keeps the finding. A container that is not running (a one shot init container that exited, or a stopped one) is reported as info, since the setting matters only when it starts. The platform's own containers (Coolify's panel stack, coolify-proxy and coolify-sentinel; Dokploy's panel, database, Redis and Traefik) keep their findings at most at warn while the platform is detected, marked as managed by the platform, because the panel does not let you change them; privileged stays a fail.

## Verify by hand

```sh
docker ps -q | xargs docker inspect --format '{{.Name}} {{range .Mounts}}{{.Source}} {{end}}' | grep -E 'docker.sock| /var/run | /run | /var | / '
```

## How to fix it

Remove the socket mount. If the container needs to read Docker state, put a socket proxy in front (for example tecnativa/docker-socket-proxy with only CONTAINERS=1) and point the container at it.

## What a fix can break

Features that use the Docker API from inside the container (service discovery, auto updates, log shipping) stop until they use a socket proxy.
